annotation.title_clean: Debunking Robot Rights Metaphysically, Ethically, and Legally
annotation.title_en: Debunking Robot Rights Metaphysically, Ethically, and Legally
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Birhane, A.; van Dijk, J.; Pasquale, F.
annotation.summary_en: Preprint arguing against robot rights on metaphysical, ethical and legal grounds. It holds that machines cannot hold rights, that limits on machines and duties on corporations should replace rights talk, and that robot rights resemble corporate rights, risking immunity from accountability for harmful AI and robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Machines are not the kind of entity that can be granted or denied rights (phenomenological, enactive view).
Ethics debate should centre on limits on machines and harms to marginalized groups, not machine rights.
Robot rights are best analogized to corporate rights, which undermined workers, consumers and voters.
Robot rights discourse risks shielding AI developers from legal accountability.
Shift focus to duties and responsibilities of corporations profiting from sociotechnical systems.
